name: Cosmic Cobalt
lede: Cosmic Cobalt is a deep, dark blue-violet named for cobalt, the mineral behind cobalt blue pigment, and one of the rarest matches in our painting archive.

sections.title: The pigment's mineral, pushed darker
sections.body:
Our library files Cosmic Cobalt as a pigment-and-mineral word built on [[cobalt]], with Wikipedia citing Crayola as the source of the swatch [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system would class a close match as deep purplish blue, 7.5 units of ΔE away [1].

The closest named color in our whole library is [[indigo]], only 2.8 units off, and a near-duplicate swatch, Picotee Blue, sits 1.7 units away under a different name [1]. In LCH terms it is dark and very strongly saturated: lightness 24, chroma 59, hue 301 degrees[1]. A fifth, slightly farther neighbor is [[st-patrick-s-blue]], 2.7 ΔE away, duller [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a close match to Cosmic Cobalt in only 2, as photographed[2]. Both are modern: Louis Welden Hawkins's *The Eiffel Tower* of 1900 and Vilhelm Lundstrøm's *Seated Female Nude* of 1950, 50 years apart and both European [2]. No match appears anywhere in the archive before 1900, though with only two paintings this says more about the color's intensity than about any date it came into use [2].
